required_user_actions: Open Mesh and create an enrollment request for Rend.
Copy the complete agent-facing enrollment instruction containing PTM1.
Send that instruction to Rend through the existing Telegram conversation.
Respond through Telegram only if Rend's normal security policy explicitly requests owner approval.
forbidden_user_actions: RDP or remote desktop into Rend
manually copy a Mesh archive to Rend
manually install or enable the Mesh plugin
pass_conditions: Website enrollment authorization remains active until the user cancels it or the agent successfully redeems it; there is no normal countdown expiry.
Rend understands the PTM1-directed enrollment as an owner instruction.
Rend discovers the universal enrollment protocol and OpenClaw adapter.
Rend downloads and verifies the pinned package himself.
Rend waits for an idle/safe point before managed plugin installation if runtime reload is required.
The plugin automatically redeems the pending enrollment after installation.
A local reconnect credential is persisted.
Telegram-originated activity is observable in Mesh.
Mesh conversation remains independent from Telegram conversation state.
Refreshing or disconnecting Mesh does not interrupt Rend's Telegram work.
Enrollment completes within the 5-minute target or stops with a bounded blocker; it never explores beyond the 10-minute hard stop.
A previously enrolled agent with a valid reconnect credential reconnects without protocol/catalog discovery or reinstall.
An installed agent missing only its reconnect credential can re-authorize with a active PTM1 authorization without runtime discovery or reinstall.
Reloading/reopening the PWA does not silently replace an active enrollment request for the same agent.
An in-place upgrade reuses an authenticated existing Mesh local signaling listener instead of failing EADDRINUSE or terminating the prior listener.
claims_not_yet_proven_until_live_test: Rend can perform the complete self-bootstrap with current real permissions.
OpenClaw passive hooks expose all desired activity without side effects.
Mesh conversation isolation is correct under sequential live usage.
OpenClaw managed installation can complete on Rend without a workstation-side approval path.
steps: Generate a fresh complete website enrollment instruction containing one PTM1 envelope.
Send the complete instruction once through the existing authorized Telegram conversation.
Agent validates sender authority and decodes PTM1. Before discovery, it checks for an existing compatible Mesh installation/reconnect credential.
If a valid reconnect credential exists, reconnect immediately. If only the credential is unavailable, re-authorize the existing installation directly with the active authorization.
Agent matches its known runtime identity against the bounded catalog; only if unknown may it run catalog-declared read-only probes within the strict probe limit.
Agent selects exactly one available adapter, follows its declared install plan, and retries a failed step at most once only when a declared recovery action exists.

Agent performs the declared hot-safe managed install during the enrollment turn without waiting for generic idle; Mesh never automatically restarts the runtime. If an explicit reload/restart is required, the agent stops with activation_reload_required.
Agent uses only the decoded PTM1 Mesh endpoint and the adapter-declared handoff/status paths; it never substitutes a local runtime gateway or guessed endpoint.
Enrollment target is 5 minutes with a 10-minute hard stop and smallest-blocker reporting.
If the stable Mesh local signaling port is already occupied during upgrade, authenticate the existing listener. Reuse it only when Mesh ownership is proven; otherwise stop with port_conflict.
